cohort: The cohort consisted of 280 fathers whose wives recently gave birth in Seka Town, Southwest Ethiopia.
finding: Paternal postpartum depression was found to be high (19.6%) and was significantly associated with a history of depression, unplanned pregnancy, alcohol consumption, infant sleeping problems, and mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was significantly associated with paternal postpartum depression (AOR: 3.0, 95% CI = [1.3, 7.6]).
cross-section timing: The study was conducted from July 7 to 17, 2023, among fathers whose wives gave birth, but the specific timing after birth for the assessment of paternal postpartum depression is not mentioned.
